references.text: The water at the Red Sea was divided when Moses stretched out his hand, just as the water in the Jordan was divided for the Israelites. Both events show God's power over water to save His people.
The water stood like a wall at the Red Sea, in the same way that the water in the Jordan stood like a heap when the Israelites crossed over.
The psalm describes how the sea fled and the Jordan turned back, as a poetic reference to Israel's crossing of the Red Sea and the Jordan.
Joshua explains that the Lord dried up the Jordan before the Israelites, just as He had done with the Red Sea.
Elijah divided the water in the Jordan by striking it with his cloak, as a parallel to the dividing of the Jordan under Joshua.
Elisha also divided the Jordan in the same way as Elijah, recalling the original crossing under Joshua.
The verse predicts that the waters coming from above will stop and stand like a heap, which is fulfilled in verse 16.
Isaiah refers to God's power to divide the water before His people, as a reminder of the deliverance from Egypt and the entry into Canaan.
